How the foundations build up

5,096 definitions and theorems (3,648 theorems) in eleven parts, all checked by Lean's kernel with no axioms beyond propositional extensionality, quotients and choice. Arrows point from what is used to what uses it.

The eleven parts

Solid arrows are real imports: one part's proofs call another's, and the thickness shows how often. Dashed arrows are the bridges: parts that use Lean's built-in natural numbers and integers are licensed to do so by the theorems proving those built-ins isomorphic to the from-scratch constructions (ω ≅ ℕ in Sets; Peano ℕ ≅ ℕ and ℤ ≅ ℤ in Numbers).

imports (thicker = more uses)bridge theorem

Every chapter

Each box is one Lean file; ★ marks files with headline results. The diagram reads left to right, from first principles to the deepest results, with redundant arrows removed (if A leads to B and B to C, the direct A→C arrow is dropped). Orange arrows cross from one part into another. Hover a box for its size.

Generated from the compiled Lean environment by scripts/module_graph.py (Graphviz) in the foundations repository.
